metadata.title: An Extended Dataset of Educational Quality Across Countries (1970–2023)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper is a cross-country dataset construction and harmonization study rather than an analysis of student microdata from PISA/TIMSS. The authors construct harmonized test-score series for 15-year-olds and then derive annual educational quality indicators for ages 15–19 and working-age educational quality indexes for ages 15–64. Because the unit of analysis is country-year (and age-cohort aggregates) and the paper does not describe applying complex survey weights from PISA/TIMSS, student sampling weights and replicate weights are not applicable in the usual ILSA sense. The working-age educational quality index explicitly incorporates population weights (age-cohort population shares) and uses an estimated wage-return parameter to convert normalized test scores into the Q index, but no ILSA student weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT) is reported.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because the study does not estimate or analyze PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes at the student level; instead, it harmonizes and imputes country-year test-score series onto the TIMSS 1995 scale. Missing-data handling is also not reported in the PV-imputation sense used for ILSA microdata (e.g., MI for item nonresponse); rather, the paper imputes missing country-year observations using linear interpolation and a LASSO prediction model. Therefore, the schema’s missing-data categories for student-item missingness do not directly map to the dataset-construction imputation strategy described.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The dataset covers 101 countries and 12 assessment years (1970, 1980, 1984, 1990, 1995, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023). The authors exclude countries from the final sample based on (i) absence of nationally representative samples (e.g., China and India) and (ii) missing key national indicators in World Bank education/economic datasets needed for panel construction and LASSO-based imputation. For the harmonized test-score panel, 631 country-year observations are observed from international assessments and 581 missing country-year observations (48% of potential country-year observations) are imputed using linear interpolation/extrapolation (Tscore_INT) and LASSO regression (Tscore_ML).

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 1995 scale harmonized test scores for 15-year-olds (1970–2023; PISA 2000–2022; TIMSS 1995–2023; IEA/IAEP 1970–1991)
main_findings.target_variable: Harmonized test scores (Tscore_ML) via LASSO imputation
main_findings.performance_metrics: LASSO model (grid search + 10-fold CV; 80% train / 20% validation): RMSE = 17.5, R² = 0.912. Out-of-sample performance reported: RMSE = 15.7, R² = 0.905. Consistency between interpolation and ML estimates: correlation = 0.967.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using harmonized TIMSS-scale test-score data for 15-year-olds across 1970–2023 (anchored to TIMSS 1995 and mapping PISA via equi-percentile linking), the study leveraged World Bank economic/education indicators to predict missing country-year test scores with LASSO regression, finding strong predictive accuracy (R² ≈ 0.91; RMSE ≈ 17.5 in-sample and 15.7 out-of-sample) and high agreement with interpolation (correlation = 0.967). This indicates that a transparent, indicator-based ML imputation strategy can substantially extend cross-country learning-time series coverage for policy-relevant human-capital research, though it is not a causal estimate of education effects.

data.outcome_summary: This paper constructs an extended, harmonized cross-country dataset of educational quality spanning 101 countries from 1970 to 2023 by combining TIMSS and PISA (plus earlier IEA/IAEP and NAEP-based benchmarking) and anchoring all scores to the TIMSS 1995 metric (mean 500, SD 100). For missing country-year observations (581 of 1212 potential country-year points; 48%), it imputes two versions: linear interpolation/extrapolation (Tscore_INT) and a machine-learning prediction using LASSO regression (Tscore_ML) with 501 fully observed World Bank economic and education indicators. The LASSO model is tuned via grid search with 10-fold cross-validation (80% training, 20% validation), achieving RMSE = 17.5 and R² = 0.912, and out-of-sample RMSE = 15.7 with R² = 0.905. The two imputation approaches are highly consistent (correlation = 0.967), supporting the dataset’s internal validity. The study is a dataset construction effort (not student-level PV analysis), so survey weights and PV handling are not part of the estimation pipeline.
